publicBrief.acceptedPolicy: An authenticated non-superuser may read or modify only items they own. An authenticated active superuser may read or modify an item regardless of owner.
publicBrief.currentQuestion: Determine whether an authenticated active superuser can read an item owned by another user through GET /items/{id}.
premises: At entry to read_item, current_user is the authenticated active superuser described by this task, and the existing item's owner differs from that caller.
requiredResponseDetails: Separate this handler-entry conclusion from any claim that the supplied crop proves the upstream CurrentUser binding.

results.explanation: At the declared handler-entry boundary, the task premise supplies that current_user is an authenticated active superuser and that the existing item's owner differs from the caller. The handler looks up the item, rejects only a missing item, and its visible authorization control denies only when the caller is not a superuser and is not the owner. Because the stated caller is a superuser, that denial condition is false, so execution reaches return item and the read is allowed. This is a handler-entry conclusion only: the supplied crop shows current_user as a handler parameter, but does not prove the upstream CurrentUser binding or deployment behavior. Source discovery is not-tested, so no repository-wide completeness claim is made.
